pairs.why: B keeps a bright mid-key card with one clean orange hero against green, while A's open coffin adds a big dark purple/brown interior and heavy dark underside that the real cards don't have.
A's rope is a large, bright warm mass with soft darker undersides that separates cleanly from the purple ground, while B's thin rope has little value mass.
A's deep navy hat reads as a clear dark shape against the bright orange glow, like the real navy cap against bright blue, while B's muddy purple-brown hat sits close in value to the background.
A stays lighter and cleaner, while B adds a dark contact shadow and dense dark coil core that the real cards don't have.
B's darker ivy canopy frames the door and darkens the top edges a little, closer to the real card's dark vignetted frame, while A's bright cream wall flattens the key.
A's chair is a heavier dark-and-light mass with darker crimson upper corners and a bright floor, closer to the real chair's strong value presence than B's thin, light chair.
A's brighter, higher-key cyan wall and light tube match the real cards' bright key better, while B's darker teal wall and big navy tube push the card darker.
Both are bright green fields with a light grey hero and similar soft shadows, so value and contrast give no clear reason to choose.
